title: Laparoscopic Antireflux Surgery Versus Endoscopic Full-thickness Gastroplication for Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
brief_summary: Endoscopic full thickness gastroplication (Plicator-Procedure) has the potential to be a safe and effective alternative to laparoscopic antireflux surgery (LARS)to improve symptoms of GERD. This prospective randomized study compares objective and subjective outcome parameters of Plicator with that of LARS.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* long history of GERD symptoms
* persistent or recurrent symptoms despite optimal medical treatment
* persistent or recurrent complications of GERD
* reduced quality of life owing to increasing esophageal exposure to gastric juice
* pathological values in the preoperative evaluated functional parameters.

Exclusion Criteria:

* any distinct hiatal hernia detectable by gastroscopy or barium radiography
* dysphagia
* esophageal strictures
* poor physical status (American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) scores III and IV) and pregnancy.
